observation: The Kitchen 3 slat assembly contained twelve valid physical slats, but its rectangular ownership container was also rendered with an opaque fill and complete perimeter. The container therefore introduced a false continuous floor line and visually occupied the open intervals between slats.
cause: Component extent and visible construction were represented by the same polygon-rendering behavior. The WD01 annotation was attached at assembly level without an explicit material-owner distinction, allowing a grouping boundary to be mistaken for a physical wood surface.
proposed_rule: Treat assembly bounds as ownership and extent data unless source evidence independently authorizes a visible fill or perimeter; attach material labels to their actual rendered owners; preserve intentional gaps; and validate actual exports for connecting strokes, covering fills, and missing child edges.
adopted_rules: Assembly or group bounds do not automatically create a visible perimeter or opaque fill.
Each visible fill and physical edge must have an evidenced owner distinct from a non-rendering assembly container.
Material codes describe the components they identify and do not authorize geometry across intentional gaps.
Validate open intervals in exported SVG, PNG, and rasterized PDF while separately confirming that every required child edge remains complete.
verification_scope: A200 Kitchen 3 revision 04; source/revision/candidate comparison, component ownership checks, three floor-gap export mutations, SVG/PNG/vector PDF, rasterized PDF, and two-build repeatability.
exclusions: No project-specific slat count, width, spacing, or A200 geometry becomes a universal default.
Effective Version skill 3 and earlier frozen restoration points remain unchanged.
